officialTitle: Pertuzumab plus trastuzumab plus docetaxel for metastatic breast cancer

design.sampleSizeSourceQuote: We randomly assigned 808 patients with HER2-positive metastatic breast cancer to receive placebo plus trastuzumab plus docetaxel (control group) or pertuzumab plus trastuzumab plus docetaxel (pertuzumab group) as first-line treatment
design.notes: Final OS analysis reported separately; crossover from placebo to pertuzumab permitted after the interim OS analysis.

clinicalQuestion: Does adding pertuzumab (dual HER2 blockade) to trastuzumab and docetaxel improve outcomes as first-line therapy for HER2-positive metastatic breast cancer?

pico.population: HER2-positive metastatic breast cancer, no previous chemotherapy or anti-HER2 therapy for metastatic disease
pico.outcomes: Primary: independently assessed PFS. Secondary: OS, investigator-assessed PFS, ORR, safety

publications.title: Pertuzumab plus trastuzumab plus docetaxel for metastatic breast cancer.
publications.label: Primary analysis

publications.title: Pertuzumab, trastuzumab, and docetaxel in HER2-positive metastatic breast cancer.
publications.label: Final prespecified OS analysis

outcomes.sourceQuote: The median progression-free survival was 12.4 months in the control group, as compared with 18.5 months in the pertuzumab group (hazard ratio for progression or death, 0.62; 95% confidence interval, 0.51 to 0.75; P<0.001).

The median overall survival was 56.5 months (95% confidence interval [CI], 49.3 to not reached) in the group receiving the pertuzumab combination, as compared with 40.8 months (95% CI, 35.8 to 48.3) in the group receiving the placebo combination (hazard ratio favoring the pertuzumab group, 0.68; 95% CI, 0.56 to 0.84; P<0.001), a difference of 15.7 months.
Median progression-free survival as assessed by investigators improved by 6.3 months in the pertuzumab group (hazard ratio, 0.68; 95% CI, 0.58 to 0.80).

safety.description: Safety profile generally similar between groups with no increase in left ventricular systolic dysfunction; grade 3 or higher febrile neutropenia and diarrhoea more frequent with pertuzumab
safety.sourceQuote: The safety profile was generally similar in the two groups, with no increase in left ventricular systolic dysfunction; the rates of febrile neutropenia and diarrhea of grade 3 or above were higher in the pertuzumab group than in the control group.

strengths: Large placebo-controlled randomised phase III trial
Final OS analysis published with long follow-up; crossover-adjusted sensitivity analyses consistent
limitations: OS was a secondary endpoint; the primary publication reported only an interim OS trend
Crossover after the interim analysis may dilute the OS difference

clinicalImplications.text: Established dual HER2 blockade with pertuzumab and trastuzumab plus a taxane as a first-line backbone for HER2-positive metastatic breast cancer, with an overall survival benefit in the final analysis.

tumourBoardPearl.text: Dual antibody blockade added efficacy without added cardiac toxicity in CLEOPATRA; watch for diarrhoea and febrile neutropenia during the docetaxel phase.

curation.notes: Numbers transcribed from PubMed abstracts of PMID 22149875 (primary) and PMID 25693012 (final OS). Publication year taken from PubMed metadata date (2011-12-07 online).
